newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIAN BROKERS CAUTIOUS ON SINGLE MARKET.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIAN BROKERS CAUTIOUS ON SINGLE MARKET.

text.p: Lithuanian brokers on Thursday said they were cautious about the formation of a unified Baltic stock settlement system in the short-term but were in favour of the idea in the longer-term.

The Lithuanian and Latvian central depositories earlier today said that Lithuanian brokers were delaying the signing of an agreement between Lithuania and the other two Baltic states that would allow the settlement of securities of each country's stocks in all the home markets.
Such an agreement has already been signed between Latvia and Estonia and is due to come into force in the summer.
Saulius Racevicius, head of Vilnius Bank's brokerage department, said that the main beneficiary of such a deal now would be Estonian brokers.
"An immediate joining (of the depositories) would be beneficial to the Estonian brokerages which have exhausted their securities market already," he told Reuters.
He added that Lithuanian brokers had little interest in the Estonian markets but Estonian broker clients interested in Lithuanian were already working with Lithuanian brokers.
"The Lithuanian broking community is cautious until they reach the same standards of service as Estonians and they are sure they will catch up in a year at most," he added.
Vilfima's head of market research Sirgitas Petraitis also said that the Lithuanian firms needed to increase their strength before the formation of a unified Baltic settelement system.

"We are sure that sooner or later the securities market of the three Baltic countries will become closer and it is apparent that Estonian financial intermediaries have advanced further," he told Reuters.
He said that if the Estonians enter the market then it would more difficult for local brokers and that most of the competing would be done by the bigger Lithuanian brokers.
"We need to make ourselves stronger to compete successfully," he added.
